thread.title: UnitedHealthcare has added Apple Watch to its wellness plan (UNH, AAPL)

author: Nicky Lineaweaver
title: UnitedHealthcare has added Apple Watch to its wellness plan (UNH, AAPL)

organizations.name: business insider intelligence " digital health brie

text:
This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence " Digital Health Briefing " subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here .
UnitedHealthcare, the US' largest insurer, has incorporated the Apple Watch into its wearable-based workplace wellness program, dubbed Motion, that's designed to reduce healthcare costs. UnitedHealthcare announced the collaboration earlier this year but hadn't made the Apple Watch available in the program until this week.
Business Insider Intelligence Now, participants can either use an existing Apple Watch or purchase a new one, with the option to pay off the device within six months using program rewards earned for meeting daily activity goals.
The collaboration's a big win for Apple, which is targeting the insurance industry as a way to drive Watch sales:
Motion could help Apple push Watch penetration among older consumers. Apple indicated it's interested in improving Watch sales among older consumers when it launched the Watch Series 4 in September with a host of senior-focused medical features. Members with chronic disease — who tend to be older — have particularly high participation rates in Motion, UnitedHealthcare notes. Motion and similar wellness programs could provide a channel for Apple to tap into the 22% of Americans ( 86 million people) will be 65 years or older by 2050, up from 15% in 2016. And these employer and insurer partners will endorse Apple products to drive usage among their members. Since these firms have a vested interest in encouraging consumers to use their fitness devices, they can essentially act as advertising agents for Apple. Apple was also reportedly in talks in August 2017 to introduce the Apple Watch to Aetna's 23 million members, which would provide another revenue bump. Apple Watch integration should strengthen UnitedHealthcare's appeal to employer clients. Employers have embraced wearables as a tool to cut employee healthcare costs — 90% of wellness programs will include fitness trackers in 2021, up from 60% in 2017, according to Gartner. Given that the Apple Watch is currently the most popular wearable device — Apple topped the global wearable market with 17% of all shipments in Q2 2018 — adding the Watch to Motion should serve as a value-add to the insurer.
Enterprises are emerging as a driving force in the booming wearable market.In addition to the pervasiveness of employers' wellness programs, life insurance companies are also spurring adoption. John Hancock announced in September that it will only sell interactive life insurance policies predicated on fitness and health data captured in wearables and smartphones.
And Greenhouse Life Insurance and Amica Life are offering qualifying members $1,000 of accidental death insurance coverage for free if they agree to share wearable data via a mobile app, per a blog post from digital health startup Cardiogram. Wearable investments by enterprises will help propel the total US installed base of fitness tracker and health-based wearables to grow at an annualized rate of 10% to surpass 120 million by 2023, per Business Insider Intelligence estimates.
